body:
## Pull request overview

This PR enhances the DetailView component with Airtable-inspired features including a functional More menu, Share button, Favorite toggle, copy-to-clipboard on field values, and improved visual design. The changes also add optional `showBorder` and `headerColor` properties to `DetailViewSection` for customization.

**Changes:**
- Enhanced DetailView header with functional More menu containing Duplicate/Export/History/Delete actions
- Added Share button with Web Share API and clipboard fallback
- Added Favorite toggle with star icon
- Added copy-to-clipboard functionality on all field values with hover-revealed buttons
- Added field count badges and improved section header styling
- Extended DetailViewSection type with showBorder and headerColor properties

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 10 comments.

Dynamic class names using template literals like `bg-${section.headerColor}` won't work correctly with Tailwind CSS. Tailwind's JIT compiler needs to see complete class names at build time to generate the CSS. This will result in the background color not being applied.

Instead, you should either:
1. Use a mapping of allowed values to complete class names
2. Accept the complete class name from the schema (e.g., "bg-muted", "bg-primary/10")
3. Use the `clsx` utility with explicit conditions for each supported color

Example fix:
```typescript
className={cn(section.headerColor)}
```

And update the type documentation to specify users should pass complete Tailwind class names.
```suggestion
          <CardHeader className={cn(section.headerColor)}>
```

Dynamic class names using template literals like `bg-${section.headerColor}` won't work correctly with Tailwind CSS. Tailwind's JIT compiler needs to see complete class names at build time to generate the CSS. This will result in the background color not being applied.

Instead, you should either:
1. Use a mapping of allowed values to complete class names
2. Accept the complete class name from the schema (e.g., "bg-muted", "bg-primary/10")
3. Use the `clsx` utility with explicit conditions for each supported color

Example fix:
```typescript
className={cn(
  "cursor-pointer hover:bg-muted/50 transition-colors",
  section.headerColor
)}
```

And update the type documentation to specify users should pass complete Tailwind class names.
```suggestion
            section.headerColor
```

This PR removes all examples/hotcrm package dependencies from the lockfile, which is not mentioned in the PR description. The PR description focuses on DetailView enhancements, not dependency cleanup.

This appears to be unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR. If this is intentional cleanup, it should be mentioned in the PR description. If it's unintentional, this could break builds that depend on the hotcrm submodule packages.

Additionally, several packages are being marked as optional (ts-node, @tsconfig/*, etc.) which could affect build behavior.

The new features added in this PR lack test coverage:
- Share button functionality (lines 136-150)
- Favorite toggle (lines 167-169, 200-218)
- More menu dropdown and its actions (Duplicate, Export, View History, Delete in menu)
- Copy-to-clipboard functionality in DetailSection

The existing test file shows that this repository has comprehensive test coverage for DetailView features (15+ tests). According to the stored memory about test coverage, the repo uses comprehensive automated testing with 3,535+ tests.

New behavior should include tests for:
1. Share button click handling and fallback behavior
2. Favorite toggle state changes
3. More menu opening and menu item clicks
4. Proper handling of navigator.clipboard and navigator.share APIs (with mocks)

The PR description claims "+2KB gzipped bundle impact" and "Enhanced Storybook stories" as testing evidence, but unit tests are needed for these interactive features.
```suggestion
    setIsFavorite((prev) => !prev);
  }, []);
```

The Share button (and other icon-only buttons) lack proper ARIA labels for screen readers. While tooltips are present, they don't provide accessible labels when the tooltip isn't visible.

Icon-only buttons should include `aria-label` attributes for accessibility:

```typescript
<Button 
  variant="outline" 
  size="icon" 
  onClick={handleShare}
  aria-label="Share record"
>
  <Share2 className="h-4 w-4" />
</Button>
```

This affects:
- Share button (line 238)
- Back button (line 190)
- Favorite toggle (line 202-212)
- More actions button (line 263)

The Tooltip component provides visual assistance but doesn't replace semantic HTML accessibility attributes.

This documentation file contains Chinese text in line 5, which violates the repository's English-only codebase policy (Copilot Instruction Rule #-1).

While the Chinese text is quoted as the "Original" request and immediately followed by an English translation, documentation files should be entirely in English. Consider either:
1. Removing the Chinese text entirely and keeping only the English translation
2. Moving the Chinese text to a separate internal planning document outside the repository

The English-only policy applies to all user-facing text, documentation, and comments in the codebase to ensure global accessibility.
